slot.brief: Charged conductor or symmetric distribution (sphere/cylinder); use Gauss's law to reason where the field is zero or which surface encloses the charge — conceptual symmetry selection.

stem: An infinitely long uniformly charged wire coincides with the axis of a closed cylindrical Gaussian surface. Its flat ends are perpendicular to the wire. What fraction of the total electric flux passes through the curved surface?

verdicts.working: The electric field of the wire is radial. It is parallel to the curved surface’s outward normal and perpendicular to the end-cap normals, so all flux passes through the curved surface.

working:
$\vec E$ is radial, so $\vec E\cdot d\vec A=0$ on each flat end.\
Thus all the flux crosses the curved surface: $\dfrac{\Phi_{\text{curved}}}{\Phi_{\text{total}}}=1$.

Independent check: The electric field of the wire is radial. It is parallel to the curved surface’s outward normal and perpendicular to the end-cap normals, so all flux passes through the curved surface.
solution:
The field of an infinitely long charged wire is radial. It is perpendicular to the end-cap normals, so the flux through the flat ends is zero.
$$\frac{\Phi_{\text{curved}}}{\Phi_{\text{total}}}=1$$
